member.name: T:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver
member.summary:
Resolve the value stored in .
Supported formats:
"~VarName" Reference a named variable (VariablesHelper).
"Vector3.up", "Color.red", "Quaternion.identity", "Physics.DefaultRaycastLayers", "Physics.AllLayers" Well-known aliases or static field refs.
"EnumValue" For enum-typed fields, maps by name.
"0,0,10,10" Comma-separated numeric args inferred from the field type: RectInt(x,y,width,height) Rect(x,y,width,height) Vector2(x,y) Vector3(x,y,z) Vector2Int(x,y) Vector3Int(x,y,z) BoundsInt(x,y,z,sizeX,sizeY,sizeZ)
numeric literals / LayerMask / TypeReference e.g. DefaultValue(3) on a LayerMask field

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver.ResolveValue(HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.MemberMetaData)
member.summary: Production entry point: called wherever MemberMetaData is available.

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver.ResolveValue(System.Type,System.Object)
member.summary: Testable entry point that doesn't require MemberMetaData. This is what you call in unit tests.

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver.ResolveStringValue(System.Type,System.String)
member.summary: Handle all string-based defaults. Order matters: we try most explicit first.

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver.ResolveLiteralValue(System.Type,System.Object)
member.summary: Handle non-string defaults like numbers, LayerMask ints or TypeReference targets.

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver.TryParseImplicitArgsForType(System.Type,System.String,System.Object@)
member.summary:
"Comma arg list" parser. We infer meaning from the target dataType.
Supported mappings: RectInt(x,y,width,height) "0,0,10,20" Rect(x,y,width,height) "0,0,1,1" Vector2(x,y) "1.5,2.25" Vector3(x,y,z) "0,1,0" Vector2Int(x,y) "3,4" Vector3Int(x,y,z) "1,2,3" BoundsInt(x,y,z,sizeX,sizeY,sizeZ) "0,1,2,10,20,30"

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.DefaultValueResolver.TryResolveStaticField(System.String,System.Object@)
member.summary:
Resolve "TypeName.FieldName" from static fields, e.g. "Physics.DefaultRaycastLayers" or "Physics.AllLayers".
This is a last-ditch: we only try it if the text didn't match an alias or implicit tuple. That lets you expose static constants from engine code or your own utility classes.

member.name: T:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.NodeSpaceInserter
member.summary: Inserts space into a node layout, e.g., before pasting or creating nodes.
member.remarks:
Goals:
- Make space to insert new nodes without overlapping existing nodes.
- Preserve the relative spacing of any moved nodes (e.g., don't squash them together).
- Minimal impact on existing layout (e.g., don't move nodes that don't need to be moved).
- Preserve GroupNode grouping (e.g., don't inadvertently add/remove nodes from the group).

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.NodeSpaceInserter.InsertSpace(UnityEngine.Vector2,UnityEngine.Rect)
member.summary: Insert space at a point. Nodes will be moved away from this point.
member.param: The point to insert space at.
Rect representing the amount of space to add, centered on atPoint.

member.name: M:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.NodeSpaceInserter.InsertSpace(UnityEngine.Vector2,UnityEngine.RectOffset)
member.summary: Insert space at a point. Nodes will be moved away from this point.
member.param: The point to insert space at.
Space that we need around the insert point.
member.remarks:
The strategy (see goals):
- If there are no overlaps in a given direction, don't move any nodes in that direction.
- Set the offset in a direction to be the largest overlap in that direction.
- Expand groups to avoid pushing nodes out of groups.

member.name: T:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.FsmGraphView
member.summary: Extends GraphView to edit Fsm Nodes.
member.remarks:
NOTE: We avoid using SerializedObject here because:
An EditorWindow can only (reliably) bind to a single SerializedObject. So it would limit our ability to show multiple FSMs etc.
Binding is slow. Binding every node in the graph would probably slow the editor down unacceptably.
It's quicker to just call as needed.
We subscribe to Fsm.Changed to update the UI. So any change to an Fsm that needs a UI update (e.g., adding/removing events) should raise the Fsm.Changed event.

member.name: T:HutongGames.PlayMaker.Editor.ProjectDatabase

summary.para:
A project database built using serialized records.
Records have a hierarchy that mirrors the organization in Unity.
E.g., SceneRecord > GameObjectRecord > ComponentRecord...

We organize the database into top level root records:
Scenes, Prefabs, Templates, Globals Events, Global Variables.
Loaded scenes are shown under a Hierarchy root record.

member.remarks: SceneRecords are updated while loaded.

member.summary: Base class for VariableRef and VariableVar fields.
member.remarks:
There are 2 main scenarios to support. 1. Concrete immutable references: [SerializeField] private FloatRef _float; 2. SerializeReference base type reference: [SerializeReference] private AnyVariableRef _variable; SerializeReference fields MUST have either:
- [BaseTypeAttribute] that defines a base data type that references must derive from.
- [MatchTypeAttribute] that defines another field that this field should get a target data type from.

member.name: T:HutongGames.Editor.CategoryListView
member.summary: Base class for searchable list views similar to Unity's AdvancedDropdown. Customization of AdvancedDropdown is limited by internal methods and classes. This class gives us better control and uses UIToolkit for easier styling etc.

ul.li: Searchable list view with category hierarchy.
Hierarchy pages can be navigated using mouse or keyboard.
Items can ignore the search filter.

remarks.para: NOTE: Uses Unity's ListView not CustomListView because we don't need special features, and we want to use item caching. E.g., Action Browser could have thousands of items.

NOTE: Uses Unity's naming convention for Selecting and Choosing items:
Selecting = highlighting the item in the list (best search result, up/down keys...).
Choosing = clicking on an item in the list.

member.remarks:
Sorting with categories can be tricky
For example:
root/move
root/move speed
root/move/isZero
root/move speed/isZero
Normal sort gives this:
root/move
root/move speed
root/move speed/isZero
root/move/isZero
We want this:
root/move
root/move/isZero
root/move speed
root/move speed/isZero

member.name: T:HutongGames.Editor.GraphView.GraphView
member.summary: An interactive GraphView based on UnityEditor.Experimental.GraphView.
member.remarks:
The Unity GraphView has some drawbacks:
It seems to be designed for a flat hierarchy, and has problems with nested nodes.
It's built around a concept of input/output edges that we don't share.
It's hard to customize built-in behaviour. E.g. grouping, snapping...
It's technically experimental and might change underneath us.
It's being replaced with GTF and might be deprecated at some point.
Hutong GraphView:
Handles hierarchical node views.
Uses transform.position for nodes (better perf).
Built for PlayMaker specific needs.

member.name: T:HutongGames.Editor.GraphView.NodeOverlapSolver
member.summary: Pushes nodes away from fixed nodes. In this context, "fixed" means nodes that the solver does not try to change. In most situations, the "fixed" nodes are actually being moved or resized.
member.remarks:
There are 2 main strategies to push nodes away:
1. Pushing nodes that intersect with fixed nodes away by enough to fix the overlap. This generally happens as part of a continuous operation, e.g., interactively moving or resizing nodes.
2. Inserting space into the layout, pushing all nodes to the left/right/up/down away from the inserted space. This preserves the relative layout of other nodes. This generally happens instantly with a big change, e.g., when pasting nodes or adding child nodes.

member.name: T:HutongGames.Editor.BaseCustomListView
member.summary: A custom ListView better suited to SerializeReference lists than the builtin Unity ListView.

remarks.para: The Unity ListView is optimized for a large number of similar items, rebinding pre-made elements to each item. This ListView is better suited to SerializeReference lists where each item can have a different UI. It also has other features not in ListView:

ul.li: Animated drag of single and multi-selections.
Supports Unity DragAndDrop from other windows.

remarks.para: NOTE: This base class does not implement editing of the underlying list data. Inheriting classes need to implement MoveItems, DeleteSelected, etc.

member.summary: Helper to quickly find VisualElements in the visual tree using a string key. Add visual elements to the dictionary when building the UI. Then later quickly find the element using its key.
member.remarks: This method can be orders of magnitude faster than UQuery. E.g., A stress test finding 150 elements in a large tree with UQuery took 800ms. Using this method it took about 2ms.

member.name: M:HutongGames.Editor.UndoHelper.FixUndoLabel(System.String)
member.summary: Set the current undo group name if it uses a generic name.
member.remarks: By default, Unity uses property paths for undo labels, which are quite ugly! This method tries to replace the default label with a custom label. This method assumes the default undo name starts with "Modified ". We could use "Modified Fsm." but that makes it very specific to PlayMaker. Hopefully Unity makes an API to inject nicer undo names in the future.
